title: Layer-aware accuracy harness with adaptive calibration and golden-corpus drift gates
creator: Ava Park
description: Goal: Implement an automated, layer-aware accuracy validation harness that combines per-layer sensitivity sweeps, adaptive calibration (per-channel and per-layer), and a golden-prompt corpus with drift detection. The harness will produce deterministic pass/fail gates used by the quantization CI pipeline and by model onboarding for runtime releases. This ticket covers design, prototype, and a CI integration for runtime-1.22. The harness must be usable for both FP8 and INT8 candidate artifacts and support: 1) per-layer perturbation simulations to detect fragile layers, 2) adaptive calibration profiles that adjust per-channel scales based on sensitivity, and 3) ensemble metrics (primary and secondary) computed against a curated golden corpus plus adversarial perturbations. The output is a machine-readable gate verdict (PASS/WARN/FAIL), a structured report with per-prompt deltas, and recommended mitigation actions (recalibrate, fallback to FP16 baseline, or suggest layer remapping). Artifacts: golden-corpus stored in s3://redwood-quant/golden-corpora/, a calibration blob format v2, and a Prometheus/Trace telemetry schema for gate events.
acceptance_criteria: 1) The harness runs end-to-end on CI for a sample INT8 and FP8 build and emits a gate verdict JSON; 2) Primary metric (BERTScore-F1) delta vs FP16 baseline is computed with bootstrap 95% CI; gate rules enforce absolute delta <= 0.8% or FAIL; 3) Secondary metrics (embedding cosine, exact-match for select prompts, generation-length distribution) computed and annotated; 4) Per-layer sensitivity table produced and stored as CSV; 5) Integration added to quantization-onboard workflow with documented remediation steps; 6) Unit/integration tests cover calibration adjustments and one adversarial perturbation scenario
approach: Phase A (design & prototype): define golden-corpus slices (sanity, edge-case, adversarial), define per-layer sweep (scale multipliers, bitwidth perturbation), and implement an extensible runner that can swap in FP8/INT8 kernels. Use a baseline run on FP16 to build reference logits/embeddings. Phase B (adaptive calibration): implement per-channel histogram-minmax + layer sensitivity weighting; produce calibration profiles that can be applied at runtime. Phase C (gating): implement statistical tests (paired bootstrap for BERTScore-F1 and bootstrap for embedding cosine) and decision logic to produce PASS/WARN/FAIL and suggested mitigation. Phase D (CI & telemetry): wire into GitHub Actions + k8s job template, emit gate events to Prometheus and push artifacts to s3. Keep the prototype language-agnostic (Python harness with a lightweight Rust micro-benchmark for perf-safe kernel invocations).
metrics: Primary: BERTScore-F1 (paired bootstrap, 95% CI) vs FP16 baseline. Gate delta threshold: absolute <= 0.8%. Secondary: mean embedding cosine similarity (candidate vs baseline) with threshold >= 0.995; exact-match percentage for retrieval-style prompts (delta <= 0.5%); generation-length distribution KL divergence threshold <= 0.02. Telemetry: per-token latency, token-level perplexity, per-layer activation drift (L2) recorded for diagnostic dashboards.
gating_policy: Verdict rules: PASS if primary metric delta <= 0.8% AND no secondary metric exceeds its threshold; WARN if primary metric delta between 0.8% and 1.5% OR one secondary metric mildly exceeds threshold; FAIL if primary metric delta > 1.5% OR any secondary metric exceeds hard limit (embedding cosine < 0.992, exact-match delta > 1.0%). On FAIL, block promotion; automatically attach recommended mitigation (re-run with per-layer FP16 override, increase calibration buckets, or fallback to FP16/FP32 model). WARNs create tickets for evaluation and require PM sign-off before promotion. Gate output schema: {verdict, primary_delta, ci_lower, ci_upper, affected_prompts: [ids], mitigation_suggestion} (exported as JSON into CI artifacts).
telemetry: Emit the following event types to Prometheus and tracing: gate_event{verdict,model,bitwidth,run_id}, prompt_delta{prompt_id,metric,delta}, layer_sensitivity{layer_id,sensitivity_score}, calibration_profile{profile_id,applied_layers}. Store verbose artifacts in s3 for 90 days: per-prompt diffs, per-layer activations, and calibration blobs. Hook trace links to Console rollout dashboards for A/B analysis.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag the harness in quantization-onboard pipeline (opt-in for now); 2) Run nightly for models in canary group (internal only) and surface WARN/FAIL to platform Slack #quant-gates; 3) After 2 weeks of stability (no false positives), enable blocking for new INT8/FP8 artifacts in runtime-1.22; 4) Post-rollout: monthly review with PM/Research to refine thresholds and expand golden-corpus. Rollback plan: revert CI gate to non-blocking and rebaseline against last-known-good FP16 blobs.
failure_modes: 1) Noisy baseline: FP16 baseline variability masks true regressions. Mitigation: increase baseline sample runs and use paired tests. 2) Golden-corpus drift: corpus no longer representative. Mitigation: corpus versioning and monthly refresh. 3) Calibration overfits to corpus and regresses unseen workloads. Mitigation: cross-validate with holdout prompt sets and adversarially perturbed prompts. 4) Performance regression when running calibration in CI. Mitigation: offload heavy runs to dedicated k8s nodes and add timeouts/approximate modes.
testing: Unit tests for calibration math (per-channel histogram logic), integration tests that run harness end-to-end against a small toy model (INT8/FP8 artifacts included), and a smoke nightly job that validates the harness itself using seeded RNG. Create synthetic adversarial set to assert harness catches a known regression. Test coverage target: 85% for harness code paths.

2026-03-08: Ran prototype against 'lama' mini-corpus: detected two fragile layers (layers 17 and 23) for the INT8 candidate; mitigation: suggested per-layer FP16 override in calibration profile.
2026-03-10: Integrated bootstrap paired test; running nightly job and pushing artifacts to s3. Observed FP16 baseline variability; added 3 baseline replicas to reduce noise.
